translation.text: Examine how the trees clothe themselves with green leaves and bear fruit. Pay attention to everything and understand how “you have made all these”—the one who lives forever.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected Ge’ez print marks “you have made all these” as corrupt. The surviving words do not yield a secure continuous sentence with “the one who lives forever.” The awkward wording is retained here as a held source-review draft, not repaired silently into “he made them all.”

source.text: ወምግባሩ፡ ቅድሜሁ፡ ለለ፡ ዓመት፡ ዘይከውን፡ ወኵሉ፡ ምግባሩ፡ ይትቀነይ፡ ሎቱ፡ ወኢይትመየጥ፡ አላ፡ በከመ፡ ሠርዐ፡ አምላክ፡ ከመዝ፡ ይትገበር፡ ኵሉ።

translation.text: His works are before him year after year. All his works obey him and do not change; everything happens just as God has ordained.

translation.text: See how the seas and rivers carry out their work together.

translation.text: But you have not persevered or kept the Lord’s command. Instead, you have transgressed and spoken great, harsh words with your impure mouths against his greatness. You dry-hearted people, you will have no peace.[a]

footnotes.text: Literally, “dry of heart,” an accusation of spiritual insensibility. “Harsh” retains the force of the selected adjective rather than importing a different wording.

source.text: ወበእንተዝ፡ አንትሙ፡ መዋዕሊክሙ፡ ትረግሙ፡ ወዓመታት፡ ሕይወት*ክሙ፡ ትኃጕሉ፡ ወ(ዓመታት፡ ኀጕልክሙ፡) ይበዝኅ፡ በርገመት፡ ዘለዓለም፡ ወኢይከውነክሙ፡ ሣህል፡

translation.text: Because of this, you will curse your days and ruin the years of your life. The years of your destruction will multiply under an everlasting curse,[a] and you will receive no mercy.

footnotes.text: Charles prints “the years of your destruction” in parentheses and says this phrase was added in accordance with his Greek witness. This draft retains the selected critical print’s supplied expression; it does not claim that it is the unqualified reading of every Ge’ez manuscript.

source.text: በውእቱ፡ መዋዕል፡ ትሁቡ፡ ስመ፡ ዚአክሙ፡ በርገመት፡ ዘለዓለም፡ ለኵሉ፡ ጻድቃን፡ ወ*ኪያክሙ፡ ይረግሙ፡ ኃጥኣን፡ . . . ዘልፈ፡ ወለክሙ፡ †ኅቡረ፡ ምስለ፡ ኃጥኣን።

translation.text: In those days you will give your name as an everlasting curse to all the righteous, and sinners will curse you. … always; and for you, together with sinners.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected print has three dots at this point and marks the final construction as corrupt. “Always,” “for you,” and “together with sinners” are surviving fragments, not a secure complete clause. No curse formula or missing words have been supplied. This draft remains held.

source.text: ወለሕሩያን፡ ይከውን፡ ብርሃን፡ ወፍሥሐ፡ ወሰላም፡ ወእሙንቱ፡ ይወርስዋ፡ ለምድር፡ ወለክሙሰ፡ ረሲዓን፡ ይከውነክሙ፡ ርገመት።

translation.text: But the chosen will have light, joy, and peace, and they will inherit the earth. But you, the wicked, will have a curse.

source.text: ወእሜሃ፡ ይትወሀቦሙ፡ ለሕሩያን፡ ጥበብ፡ ወኵሎሙ፡ እሉንቱ፡ የሐይዉ፡ ወኢይደግሙ፡ አብሶ፡ ኢበረሲዕ፡ ወኢበትዕቢት፤ አላ፡ ይገንዩ፡ ዘቦሙ፡ ጥበበ፡

translation.text: Then wisdom will be given to the chosen, and all of them will live. They will no longer sin through wickedness or pride; instead, those who have wisdom will be humble.[a]

footnotes.text: The final verb has the sense of humble submission. The selected print’s opening “then” is editorially emended; it is not represented here as an uncontested manuscript reading.

source.text: ወኢይደግሙ፡ አብሶ፡ ወኢይትኴነኑ፡ ኵሎ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ሕይወቶሙ፡ ወ*ኢይመውቱ፡ *በመቅሠፍት፡ ወኢበመዓት፡ አላ፡ ኍልቈ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ሕይወቶሙ፡ ይፌጽሙ፡ ወይሌህቅ፡ ሕይወቶሙ፡ በሰላም፡ ወዓመታተ፡ ፍሥሓሆሙ፡ ይበዝኅ፡ *በኃሤት፡ ወበሰላም፡ ዘለዓለም፡ ውስተ፡ ኵሉ፡ መዋዕለ፡ ሕይወቶሙ።

uncertainties.detail: Printed10 apparatus24 explicitly considers not-judged/not-sin alternatives and upstream corruption; retain selected judgment verb.
Printed12 apparatus2 suggests punishment-of-death wording; not adopted. The two printed negatives are retained.

translation.text: They will no longer sin, nor will they be condemned throughout all the days of their lives.[a] They will not die by punishment or wrath, but will complete the full number of their days. Their lives will grow long in peace, and their years of joy will increase in gladness and everlasting peace throughout all the days of their lives.[b]

footnotes.text: The selected Ge’ez has “will not be condemned/judged.” Its apparatus discusses a different “will not sin” reading and possible corruption. This draft retains the selected Ge’ez judgment verb rather than silently replacing it with that alternative.

The verse continues for six lines on the next Ge’ez page before chapter VI. The print retains separate “by punishment” and “not by wrath” expressions; its apparatus proposes combining them as “punishment of death.” This draft follows the printed wording instead of silently adopting the proposal.
